I localized the changes, but did not edit project source or tests: the assigned fault-localization role permits diagnosis only.

- [add_book/__init__.py](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:971): `load` needs to pass `save` through both new and matched edition paths. `load_data`, `new_work`, and the author reply helper currently allocate real keys or perform writes. Preview must collect the Edition, Work, and Author edits while skipping uploads, `save_many`, and Archive.org updates.
- [load_book.py](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/load_book.py:271): `import_author` and `build_query` are the rename points. Language conversion and typed descriptions already exist, but honorific removal happens only through `build_query`; other author paths can behave differently.
- [import API handlers](/app/openlibrary/plugins/importapi/code.py:171): direct, IA, and bulk MARC requests each need to propagate `preview=true` to `load`.

The [existing tests](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/tests/test_add_book.py) cover cover hosts, matching, and MARC imports, but contain no preview coverage. One open design point is whether a URL with an allowed hostname and an explicit port should pass: the current cover check compares the full network location, including the port. Findings are recorded in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md).

Implemented `preview=true` for the direct, IA, and bulk MARC import endpoints. Preview runs return simulated keys, a `preview: true` flag, pending Edition, Work, and Author records in `edits`, and cover acceptability without saving records, uploading covers, or updating Archive.org metadata.

I also added case-insensitive cover host validation and the requested author and edition conversion interfaces. Validation and matching run through the same import pipeline in preview and normal modes.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch has two correctness gaps:

- An allowed cover on a matched edition is skipped in preview because [update_edition_with_rec_data](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:870) only processes covers when `save=True`. The preview can report the edition as matched with no edits even though a real import would modify it. Represent the proposed cover changes without uploading.
- [Author matching](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/load_book.py:256) can merge remote IDs or add a death date, but [load_author_import_records](/app/openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:231) adds only new authors to `edits`. Include modified existing authors in both preview edits and saved edits.

**Tests:** `pytest -q openlibrary/catalog/add_book/tests/test_add_book.py openlibrary/catalog/add_book/tests/test_load_book.py openlibrary/plugins/importapi/tests` — 194 passed. These paths remain uncovered; there is no test environment problem. No project code or tests were changed during this review.

Fixed both review findings. Preview now shows an accepted cover as a pending edit on a matched edition without uploading it. Changes to existing authors, including remote IDs and death dates, now appear in preview edits and are saved during normal imports.

Added regression tests. The reviewer’s exact test command passes: **197 passed**.
